examples.en: There are many garden trees in our yard.

examples.ko: 봄마다 정원수를 다듬는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Trimming the garden trees every spring is not easy.
My father planted a pine tree as a garden tree.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 정원수 몇 그루가 쓰러졌어요.
examples.en: A few garden trees fell down because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 정원수 관리가 잘되어 있어요.
examples.en: The garden trees in this neighborhood are well maintained.

examples.ko: 정원수에 물을 주는 건 제가 맡았어요.
examples.en: I took charge of watering the garden trees.

explain: 집 마당이나 공원에 심어 가꾸는 나무를 말해요. 길가에 줄지어 심은 나무는 '가로수'라고 해서 서로 구별돼요. 일상에서는 그냥 '나무'라고도 하고, '정원수'는 나무를 관리하거나 심는 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to trees planted and cared for in a yard or park. Trees lined along a street are called '가로수', so the two are distinguished. In daily talk people often just say '나무', and '정원수' comes up mostly when talking about planting or caring for trees.

examples.en: I bought one geun of pork at the butcher shop.
The meat at this butcher shop is always fresh.
I picked out some beef at the meat section.

examples.ko: 마트 정육 코너는 저녁에 할인을 해요.
examples.en: The meat section at the mart has a discount in the evening.

examples.ko: 정육점 아저씨가 고기를 얇게 썰어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The butcher sliced the meat thinly for me.

examples.ko: 저는 주말마다 정육점에 들러 고기를 사요.
examples.en: I stop by the butcher shop every weekend to buy meat.

explain: 뼈와 기름을 발라낸 살코기를 뜻하지만, 실제로는 '정육점', '정육 코너'처럼 가게나 매장 이름으로 가장 많이 들어요. 고기를 사는 이야기에서는 '정육점에 가다'라고 말해요. 옛날식 표현으로 '푸줏간'도 있어요.
explain_en: It means meat with the bones and fat removed, but in practice you hear it most in shop names like '정육점' (butcher shop) and '정육 코너' (meat section). When talking about buying meat, people say '정육점에 가다'. An old-fashioned word for the same shop is '푸줏간'.

examples.en: We promised to compete fair and square.
This time I really want to win fair and square.
He apologized openly without hiding.
In an exam you should compete honestly on your own ability.

examples.ko: 정정당당히 말하면 아무도 뭐라고 못 해요.
examples.en: If you speak openly and honestly, nobody can say anything.
The players finished the match fairly.

explain: '정정당당하다'의 부사형이고 겨루기, 승부, 사과처럼 떳떳하게 행동하는 장면에 잘 어울려요. 반대되는 느낌은 '비겁하게'예요. 말할 때는 '떳떳하게'나 '공정하게'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is the adverb form of '정정당당하다' and fits scenes where someone acts openly and honestly, such as competing, winning or apologizing. The opposite feeling is '비겁하게' (cowardly). In speech it can often be swapped with '떳떳하게' or '공정하게'.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 옛날에 온 정착민들이 세웠어요.
examples.en: This village was founded by settlers who came long ago.
The settlers and the native people held a festival together.

examples.ko: 새로 온 정착민에게 마을 사람들이 도움을 줬어요.
examples.en: The villagers helped the newly arrived settlers.
He is a descendant of the early settlers.
The settlers lived by farming at first.

examples.ko: 정착민 마을에는 아직 오래된 집이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Old houses still remain in the settlers' village.

explain: 다른 곳에서 옮겨 와 그 땅에 자리 잡고 사는 사람을 말해요. '이주민'은 옮겨 왔다는 점에, '정착민'은 자리를 잡고 살게 된 점에 초점이 있어요. 역사나 지리 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to people who moved from elsewhere and made a life on that land. '이주민' focuses on the fact that they moved, while '정착민' focuses on their having settled down. It often appears in history and geography topics.

examples.en: That lawmaker is praised for outstanding political skill.

examples.ko: 새 총리는 이번에 정치력을 시험받고 있어요.
examples.en: The new prime minister is having their political skill tested this time.

examples.ko: 정치력 없이는 큰 개혁을 하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to carry out a big reform without political skill.
That person got through the crisis with political skill.
I think political skill is built through experience.

examples.ko: 그는 여야를 설득하는 정치력을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: He showed the political skill to persuade both the ruling and opposition parties.

explain: 사람들 사이의 이해관계를 조정하고 설득해서 일을 풀어 가는 능력을 말해요. '정치력이 있다/없다/뛰어나다'나 '정치력을 발휘하다'처럼 자주 써요. 정치인뿐 아니라 조직에서 사람들을 잘 조율하는 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means the ability to balance different interests and persuade people to get things done. It is common in phrases like '정치력이 뛰어나다' and '정치력을 발휘하다'. Besides politicians, it can describe anyone who coordinates people well in an organization.

examples.en: Political awareness among young people has risen.

examples.ko: 정치의식을 키우려면 뉴스를 꾸준히 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To build political awareness, you need to watch the news steadily.
Political awareness grows through education too.

examples.ko: 이 수업은 학생들의 정치의식에 큰 영향을 줬어요.
examples.en: This class had a big effect on the students' political awareness.
We need healthy political awareness and a sense of responsibility.
When political awareness is low, the voting rate drops too.

explain: 정치와 사회 문제에 관심을 갖고 자기 생각을 가지는 태도를 말해요. '정치의식이 높다/낮다/강하다'처럼 정도를 나타내는 말과 자주 함께 써요. 뉴스, 토론, 사회 수업에서 많이 나오는 표현이에요.
explain_en: It describes the attitude of paying attention to politics and social issues and holding your own views. It often goes with words of degree, such as '정치의식이 높다/낮다/강하다'. You will see it a lot in news, debates and social studies classes.

examples.en: The new government was plagued by a legitimacy controversy.
This restaurant is famous for the authenticity of its flavor.
Criticism keeps coming that it lacks legitimacy.

examples.ko: 전통 음식의 정통성은 어디서 찾아야 할까요?
examples.en: Where should we look for the authenticity of traditional food?

examples.ko: 정통성을 지키는 것과 변화는 다른 문제예요.
examples.en: Preserving authenticity and making changes are different matters.
If legitimacy becomes a problem, the government wavers.

explain: 정치에서는 권력이 올바른 절차로 얻어진 것인지를, 음식이나 문화에서는 원래의 방식을 제대로 이어 왔는지를 말해요. 두 경우 모두 '정통성이 있다/없다', '정통성 논란'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말인 '정당성'은 옳고 마땅하다는 점에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: In politics it asks whether power was gained by a proper process, and in food or culture it asks whether the original way has been faithfully continued. In both cases you say '정통성이 있다/없다' or '정통성 논란'. The similar word '정당성' focuses more on being right and justified.

examples.en: He is a mainstream, traditional jazz player.

examples.ko: 정통파 요리사들은 레시피를 잘 바꾸지 않아요.
examples.en: Traditionalist chefs rarely change their recipes.
I like new styles more than the traditional school.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 정통파로 불릴 만큼 방식이 엄격해요.
examples.en: This school is strict enough in its methods to be called orthodox.
The orthodox and reformist sides were at odds for a long time.
We should accept methods that are not the orthodox way too.

explain: 원래의 방식이나 가르침을 그대로 이어 가는 쪽을 말해요. 반대편은 '개혁파'나 '신세대'처럼 새로운 방식을 따르는 쪽이에요. 정치, 학문뿐 아니라 음악이나 요리, 운동 스타일 이야기에도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the side that carries on the original method or teaching as it was. The opposite side is '개혁파' or newer groups that follow new ways. It is used not only in politics and academics but also for styles of music, cooking and sports.

examples.en: People each told a different story.
The children each came running with a toy.

examples.ko: 회의가 끝나고 우리는 제가끔 집으로 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: After the meeting ended, we each went back home.
The students each gave their own opinion.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 제가끔 좋아하는 반찬이 달라요.
examples.en: In my family, everyone likes different side dishes.
The customers each ordered a different dish.

explain: '각자'와 비슷하지만, 사람들이 서로 다르게 말하거나 행동하는 모습이 느껴질 때 잘 어울려요. 보통 동사 앞에 놓아서 '제가끔 ~하다'로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '각자', '따로따로'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is close to '각자' (each person), but it fits best when you want to show people speaking or acting in different ways. It usually goes right before the verb, as in '제가끔 ~하다'. In everyday talk people more often say '각자' or '따로따로'.

examples.en: In math class I learned that the square root of 9 is 3.
Please tell me how to find a square root.
I knew right away that the square root of 16 is 4.
The square root problem was hard, so I asked my teacher.

examples.ko: 숫자의 제곱근과 제곱은 서로 반대 개념이에요.
examples.en: The square root and the square of a number are opposite concepts.

examples.ko: 시험에 제곱근 계산이 나올 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think square root calculations will be on the test.

explain: '제곱'과 짝이 되는 말로, 제곱해서 그 수가 되는 수를 찾는 개념이에요. 'a의 제곱근'처럼 말하고, 기호 √는 수업에서 '루트'라고 읽기도 해요. 수학 수업이나 시험에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is the partner of '제곱' (square): you look for the number that gives the original number when squared. You say it as 'the 제곱근 of a', and the symbol √ is also read aloud as '루트' in class. It comes up often in math lessons and exams.

examples.ko: 이 우산은 비가 오면 제구실도 못 해요.
examples.en: This umbrella can't even do its job when it rains.

examples.ko: 그 아이도 이제 제구실을 할 나이가 됐어요.
examples.en: That child has now reached an age to do their part.
There is not a single appliance at home that works properly.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 다리가 부러져서 제구실이 안 돼요.
examples.en: This chair's leg is broken, so it can't serve its purpose.

examples.ko: 동네 도서관이 제구실은 하고 있나 싶어요.
examples.en: I wonder whether the neighborhood library is even doing its job.

examples.ko: 회의가 길기만 하고 제구실을 제대로 못 했어요.
examples.en: The meeting was just long and didn't serve its purpose properly.

explain: 주로 '제구실을 하다', '제구실을 못 하다'처럼 써요. 물건이 제 기능을 하는지, 사람이 어른으로서 자기 몫을 하는지를 말할 때 모두 쓸 수 있어요. 안 될 때는 '제구실을 못 하다'가 가장 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '제구실을 하다' or '제구실을 못 하다'. You can use it both for an object doing its proper function and for a person doing their share as an adult. When something fails, '제구실을 못 하다' is the most natural way to say it.

examples.en: Darn it, I left my wallet at home.
Damn, I just missed the bus again.
Darn it, it's pouring and I don't even have an umbrella.
Darn it, I didn't get any of my homework done.
Damn, I don't know where I put my keys.

examples.ko: 제길, 오늘따라 되는 일이 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: Damn, nothing is going right today.

explain: 일이 뜻대로 안 풀려서 짜증이 날 때 혼잣말처럼 내뱉는 말이에요. 조금 거칠게 들리니까 윗사람 앞이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 피하는 게 좋아요. 비슷한 말로 '젠장'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is what you mutter to yourself when things go wrong and you are annoyed. It sounds a bit rough, so avoid it in front of elders or in formal situations. A similar word is '젠장'.

examples.ko: 문을 두드리자 그가 제꺽 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: As soon as I knocked, he opened the door right away.
When I ask a question, the answer comes back right away.
The food came out the moment I ordered.
When you give him a job, he finishes it right away.
When I called its name, the puppy came running at once.
As soon as I called my friend, they picked up right away.

explain: 망설이거나 미루지 않고 아주 재빠르게 할 때 쓰는 말이에요. '바로', '곧바로'와 비슷하지만 말할 때 쓰는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 동사 앞에 와서 '제꺽 열다', '제꺽 대답하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It describes doing something very quickly, with no hesitation or delay. It is similar to '바로' or '곧바로' but feels more like spoken language. It usually comes before a verb, as in '제꺽 열다' or '제꺽 대답하다'.

examples.en: The package arrived on the scheduled date.
It's hard to finish the construction by the due date.
Keeping to the scheduled date is the most important thing.
I sent it early so it would arrive on the right date.
My pay came in on the right date, so I'm relieved.
They kept to the date, but the item was damaged.

explain: 약속하거나 정해 둔 바로 그 날짜를 말해요. '제날짜에 맞추다', '제날짜에 도착하다', '제날짜를 지키다'처럼 자주 써요. 날짜가 아니라 시간대나 시기를 말할 때는 '제때'를 써요.
explain_en: It means the very date that was promised or set. It is common in phrases like '제날짜에 맞추다', '제날짜에 도착하다' and '제날짜를 지키다'. When you mean the proper time rather than a date, use '제때'.

examples.en: He did not receive formal, mainstream education.
There are many artists outside the establishment.
You need qualifications to get into the formal system.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 제도권과 거리를 두고 활동해요.
examples.en: That writer works while keeping a distance from the establishment.
It was hard to get a loan from the formal financial sector.

examples.ko: 제도권의 도움을 받지 못하는 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: There are people who can't get help from the official system.

explain: 법과 공식 제도가 정한 틀 안에 있는 영역을 말해요. 반대 느낌으로 '제도권 밖'이라는 말을 자주 써요. 교육, 금융, 정치, 문단처럼 공식 틀이 있는 분야에 많이 붙어요.
explain_en: It refers to the area that falls within the framework set by laws and official systems. Its opposite is often expressed as '제도권 밖' (outside the system). It is attached often to fields with an official framework, such as education, finance, politics and literature.

examples.en: The government decided to make remote work an official system.
Waste decreased after recycling separation was made an official system.

examples.ko: 이 규칙을 제도화하면 모두가 따르기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If we make this rule official, it will be easy for everyone to follow.
The company made parental leave an official system last year.

examples.ko: 좋은 관행을 제도화한 뒤에도 문제가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Problems can still arise after a good practice has been formalized.

examples.ko: 학교에서 이 활동을 제도화하자는 의견이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Opinions came up to make this activity an official program at school.

explain: 관행이나 약속을 법이나 규칙 같은 공식적인 틀로 만든다는 점에서 '정해 두다'보다 훨씬 무게가 있어요. 보통 '~을/를 제도화하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 일이 저절로 그렇게 되었을 때는 '제도화되다'를 써요. 뉴스나 보고서에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
explain_en: It carries much more weight than simply '정해 두다' because it turns a practice or agreement into an official framework like a law or rule. It is usually used as '~을/를 제도화하다', and when things become that way on their own you use '제도화되다'. You often see it in news and reports.

examples.en: You have to take your medicine on time every time to recover quickly.
I tend to pay my utility bills on time, each time.
If you do your homework on time each day, it's easier later.

examples.ko: 화분에 물을 제때제때 줬더니 잘 자랐어요.
examples.en: I watered the plant on schedule every time, and it grew well.
I wish my pay would come on time every time.

examples.ko: 메일에 제때제때 답장하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to reply to emails promptly each time.

explain: '제때'를 겹쳐 써서, 한 번이 아니라 그때그때 정해진 시간에 빠짐없이 한다는 느낌을 줘요. 약 먹기, 공과금 내기, 물 주기처럼 반복되는 일에 잘 어울려요. 한 번만 시간에 맞는 일에는 그냥 '제때'를 써요.
explain_en: It doubles '제때' to give the feeling of doing something at the proper time each time, without missing, rather than just once. It suits repeated tasks like taking medicine, paying bills or watering plants. For something that happens on time just once, use plain '제때'.
